category_title: Frustrated students with external barriers who exhibit initial off-task behavior
minimal_context: Earl arrives late to a small group after-school tutoring session and is asked to re-work math problems from class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Earl, please take a seat and start re-working the math problems from class today.

STUDENT: (Walks in 10 minutes late and talks loudly to another student) I can’t always go, like I have been twice this month only because I can’t just walk home.

TUTOR: Let's get started on the homework now.

STUDENT: My mom gets home late and doesn’t have time or know how to help me. She is usually cooking dinner or with my little brother and sister. Tutoring is kinda boring ‘cuz I know we're going to do the same stuff.

TUTOR: Just look at the problems and try your best to do them.

STUDENT: (Turns away from the assignment to distract the student next to him) Sometimes it’s just the same lesson or homework. I lose focus ‘cuz it ends up being like, a lot of math.

options.A: Break the math assignment down into smaller chunks so the problems can be completed during the session.
options.B: Directly intervene and tell the peer next to Earl, "you need to stop," during the tutoring session.
options.C: Spend approximately 10 minutes with Earl to ensure he has his class notes or takes the time to copy the tutor's notes.
options.D: Agree with Earl that he is having a rough time with the math problems and his schedule.
